subject: pharmacology
title: Opioid Respiratory Depression, Withdrawal, Constipation and Nalbuphine

steps.tx: **Respiratory depression** is mu agonism at brainstem rhythm and chemosensory circuits (pre Botzinger complex and central chemoreceptors): rate falls first, tidal volume follows, the CO2 response curve flattens and shifts right, and hypoxic drive becomes the last governor, which supplemental oxygen can silence unwitnessed. Sedation level predicts it better than any single rate number. Sleep apnoea, COPD, infancy, old age and co sedatives multiply the risk multiplicatively, not additively.
steps.say: Watch sedation, not just rate; oxygen can hide hypoventilation behind a reassuring saturation.

nodes.label: Mu agonism at brainstem respiratory circuits
CO2 responsiveness flattens and shifts right
Rate and tidal volume fall, sedation deepens first
Apnoea and hypoxic injury if unrecognised

steps.tx: **Management** climbs a ladder in order: stop further opioid, stimulate and position, give oxygen while recognising it does not ventilate, assist ventilation with bag and mask (the definitive bridge), then titrated naloxone with infusion planning for long acting agents, and continuous observation because renarcotisation outlasts most discharge impulses. Capnography detects hypoventilation that oximetry misses on oxygen, which is why monitored beds, not corridor trolleys, host high risk titration.
steps.say: Ventilate first, naloxone titrated second, and observe longer than the antagonist lasts.

left.title: Immediate ladder
points: Stop opioid, call for help, stimulate
Airway, positioning and high flow oxygen
Bag mask ventilation as the bridge
Titrated naloxone to ventilation

right.title: After stabilisation
points: Naloxone infusion for long acting agonists
Capnography where hypoventilation may hide
Observation beyond antagonist duration
Regimen redesigned before any rechallenge

steps.tx: **Opioid withdrawal** is rebound noradrenergic and cholinergic weather after dependence: early lacrimation, rhinorrhoea, yawning and anxiety (the cold turkey skin and flu mimicry), mid-course mydriasis, piloerection, vomiting, diarrhoea and cramps, with insomnia and craving throughout. Timelines follow half life (heroin and morphine 6 to 12 hours to onset, methadone 24 to 36), severity is scored (COWS), and while rarely lethal in healthy adults it kills by dehydration in custody and by relapse overdose after tolerance evaporates.
steps.say: Withdrawal feels like flu with dilated pupils; its danger is dehydration and the overdose waiting after it.

left.title: Withdrawal timetable
points: Short acting: onset 6 to 12 hours, peak 36 to 72
Methadone: onset 24 to 36 hours, weeks of tail
COWS scoring grades severity objectively
Craving outlasts physical signs

right.title: Symptomatic pharmacology
points: Clonidine or lofexidine: alpha 2 dampens noradrenergic storm
Loperamide, antiemetics, antispasmodics by symptom
Substitution induction once withdrawal declares
Relapse prevention planning from day one

steps.tx: **Constipation** is peripheral mu blockade of gut propulsion and secretion plus central contributions, the one effect with essentially no tolerance, present in up to 95 percent of chronic users without prophylaxis and capable of ileus, overflow, pseudo obstruction presentations and stercoral perforation at the extremes. Stimulant plus osmotic laxatives start with the opioid, not after impaction; peripherally restricted antagonists (previous lesson) rescue refractory cases, and bulk fibre alone in immobile patients can cement the problem it meant to soften.
steps.say: The bowel never tolerises; prescribe the laxative with the opioid, every time, from day one.

nodes.label: Stimulant and osmotic laxative co prescribed
Bowel habit reviewed at every contact

steps.tx: **Nalbuphine**, another kappa agonist mu partial antagonist, serves as analgesic where its ceiling on respiratory depression was once marketed as safety, and in small intravenous doses as a celebrated antipruritic for neuraxial opioid itching, reversing mu mediated itch while largely preserving analgesia at those doses. It precipitates withdrawal in dependence like its mixed cousins, causes sedation and dysphoria dose dependently, and shares their modern demotion to teaching and niche status.
steps.say: Nalbuphine's surviving trick is curing spinal morphine itch at doses that spare the analgesia.

left.title: Nalbuphine niches
points: Kappa agonism, mu partial antagonism
Low dose antipruritic for neuraxial opioid itch
Respiratory depression ceiling as single agent
Obstetric analgesia history

right.title: Nalbuphine limits
points: Precipitates withdrawal in mu dependence
Analgesic ceiling reached early
Sedation and dysphoria with escalation
Avoid in chronic full agonist therapy

steps.tx: **Tolerance, dependence and addiction** are three different nouns examinations weaponise: tolerance is pharmacological adaptation needing more drug for the same effect, physical dependence is withdrawal on cessation, and addiction (opioid use disorder) is compulsive use despite harm driven by reward circuitry and environment. Pain patients develop the first two predictably and the third uncommonly with structured prescribing; confusing the nouns stigmatises patients and corrupts prescribing in both directions.
steps.say: Tolerance is not dependence is not addiction; grade the vignette's noun before judging its patient.

left.title: Pharmacological adaptations
points: Tolerance: dose escalation for same effect
Physical dependence: withdrawal on stopping
Both expected with chronic exposure
Managed by tapering and regimen design

right.title: Opioid use disorder
points: Compulsive use, craving, loss of control
Continued use despite harm
Treated with substitution and psychosocial care
Not diagnosed by tolerance or dependence alone

steps.tx: **Opioid induced hyperalgesia** completes the chronic paradox: sustained high dose exposure sensitises pronociceptive systems (NMDA mediated) so pain worsens as doses climb and spreads beyond its original territory, distinguished from tolerance by distribution and allodynia and treated paradoxically by dose reduction, rotation, methadone's NMDA arm or ketamine in specialist hands. The vignette giveaway is escalating dose with expanding, unexplained pain and a normal disease review.
steps.say: Pain that grows and spreads as doses climb may be the opioid itself; sometimes less opioid is the analgesic.

nodes.label: Pain expands with allodynia beyond original site
Dose reduction or rotation improves pain

steps.tx: **Safe prescribing systems** close the module: start low with immediate release formulations, define functional goals and review dates, co prescribe laxatives and (where risk argues) naloxone, avoid benzodiazepine and gabapentinoid stacking, check prescription monitoring where available, taper when harm exceeds benefit at roughly 5 to 10 percent monthly with patient partnership, and never abandon a dependent patient for failing a regimen the system designed.
steps.say: Goals, laxatives, naloxone where risk lives, no sedative stacking, and tapers negotiated never imposed by abandonment.

left.title: Initiation safeguards
points: Functional goals and review date documented
Immediate release before modified release
Laxative and antiemetic plan attached
Sedative co prescriptions audited

right.title: Continuation safeguards
points: Benefit reviewed against goals, not scores alone
Naloxone co prescribed where overdose risk argues
Taper 5 to 10 percent monthly when harm leads
Dependence treated, never punished by abandonment
